chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man entrusts a bequest to his brother while he is absent, then he has no right to reject his executorship, because if he had been present and refused to accept it, he would have sought someone else.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: appointed through a bequest or will
key_terms.طَلَبَ غَيْرَهُ: he would have sought someone else in his place
key_terms.غَائِبٌ: absent, not present at the time of appointment
key_terms.وَصِيَّتَهُ: his bequest or executorship appointment in a will

ai.seo_question: Can a person reject being appointed executor of a will if the appointment was made in his absence?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about being appointed as an executor in a will while absent. It indicates that such an appointment is binding in this case, because had the person been present and declined, the testator could have designated another person instead.
